reviewers.summary: The round 3 change skips comment text in forward token searches, but the backward object-boundary search still treats comment text as syntax. A crafted comment can therefore bypass the stream expansion check.

findingList.message: A comment containing `endobj` can make preflight skip a real Flate stream, allowing an oversized decoded stream to reach the worker (OWASP A06:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: FindPdfToken skips PDF comments when locating `stream`, but LastIndexOfPdfToken scans backward without skipping comments to locate the preceding `endobj`. CheckStreamLimits then skips a stream when that comment token makes the object-boundary search fail.
evidence.failureScenario: A PDF contains a Flate stream whose dictionary is followed by a comment containing `endobj` before the actual `stream` keyword. The backward scan treats the comment text as the object boundary, fails to find the object's earlier `obj` token, and skips checking the stream. The parser can then start the worker on an over-limit compressed stream, violating the decoded-stream bound (OWASP A06:2025).

reviewers.summary: The fix skips repeated stream tokens in comments, but it also treats percent signs inside literal strings as comments. That can let a filtered stream bypass preflight.

findingList.message: The comment skip can miss a filtered stream marker when `%` occurs inside a PDF literal string, bypassing the decoded-stream bound (OWASP A06:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: CheckStreamLimits uses FindPdfToken to locate stream markers. The new percent handling skips to the next line without tracking whether the percent is inside a PDF literal string.
evidence.failureScenario: A valid PDF puts a literal string containing `%` before `/Length` and `/Filter /FlateDecode` in the same object-dictionary line as `stream`. The percent handler skips the rest of that line, including the real stream marker, so preflight can report the compressed bomb as safe and start the worker without enforcing the decoded-byte limit. This is a reachable resource-exhaustion risk (OWASP A06:2025).

reviewers.summary: The preflight now skips PDF comment contents while locating stream tokens, addressing the reported repeated scans. I found no remaining in-scope security defect.
